prompt: I was just turned down for a credit card. What does the Consumer Reports Complete Guide to Managing Your Money say about credit reports and what I should do now? Also, I'm married—does that affect my credit file?
assertions: Explains you are entitled to see your credit bureau file, with the fee waived if denied credit recently (within 30 days per the book)
Advises reviewing the report and disputing errors
Mentions the Equal Credit Opportunity Act 'user' designation so a married person gets credit for accounts in the spouse's name
Notes many routine payments (rent, utilities, phone, medical) are not reported to credit bureaus
Mentions current free access via annualcreditreport.com and/or FCRA dispute rights as an update to the 1989 book
Mentions skepticism toward paid credit-repair or credit-credential services
